name: Bright Data Browser API

modes.label: Bandwidth-billed browser
modes.note: No browser-time meter advertised; billed network GB. Do not interpret as a free compute VM. Unspecified guest OS is not a selectable OS guarantee.

plans.name: Free tier
plans.note: 5,000 credits/month; page says 1 GB included/month; no card.

plans.name: Pay as you go
plans.note: $8/GB, no monthly commitment, unlimited concurrent sessions.

plans.name: Scale $499
plans.note: 71 GB included; $7/GB rate in page slider data.

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.note: Custom package, SLA, SSO, audit logs.

features.ip_note: All traffic billed $8/GB pay-as-you-go (Scale $499/mo incl. 71 GB) with built-in residential proxy rotation and unlocking included.

caveats: Storage, snapshot GiB-month and public IPv4 prices are not published in the reviewed sources; null is not free.

No guaranteed vCPU allocation published; browser-hour is not a verified 4-vCPU/8-GiB VM equivalent. The sizes card keeps unknown hardware null; do not coerce it to zero or auto-rank against resource-guaranteed VMs.
Browser RAM is not published unless a specific mode overrides it.

Rendered currency widgets returned empty prices; exact USD recovered from public data-usd and data-tiers attributes in saved HTML. These are primary-page values, not guessed from the headline from-$5/GB.

Network meters browser/proxy traffic, not necessarily customer-facing VM egress. Plans have different GB pricing; strict engine cannot couple mode-specific network rates with package allowances. Card network remains null, and GB tariffs stay in raw/regime data.
Unlimited concurrency is a marketing entitlement, not verified load testing. Session lifetime/profile retention, CPU/RAM, resolution and separate recording prices remain unverified.

fleet.verification: Free Browser API zone starts without card. Robots.txt exceptions require KYC; restricted targets may require compliance permission. Standalone residential proxy network KYC must not be assumed mandatory for ordinary Browser API signup.
fleet.tiers: Pricing advertises unlimited concurrent Browser API sessions on PAYG/scaled plans.
fleet.notes: No numeric new-account concurrency cap or quota-increase SLA in inspected docs; null retains advertised-unlimited/unknown distinction. Traffic credits and compliance gates can prevent practical fleet use independently of concurrency.
